falsifier: the same artifact scored against the two corpora reads the same figure, which would mean the sitting changed nothing a score can see
hypothesis: the sitting of 2026-09-22 moved the yardstick enough that the published Baseline figures cannot be carried forward, because it dropped 41 reference claims and added 25
intervention: scored the 6bff717 Baseline artifact twice with today's scorer: once against the corpus at 6bff717 and once against the corpus at HEAD. No corpus model.json or facts.json moved in that window, so no element was re-keyed and the two scores differ only by the reference set.
reconsider_when: a corpus model.json or facts.json moves, which re-keys elements and breaks the isolation this row rests on
scope: one artifact, one scorer, two reference sets, stride only. The old-corpus score reproduces the published 0.434 reference and 0.563 must-find coverage to three decimals, which independently prices scorer drift over this window at zero. Says nothing about a sweep run today, whose prompts have moved.
signature: the Case Sitting rewrote the corpus, so no published Baseline figure is measured against the reference set that stands

falsifier: the rows carry no displaced draft, or the cause names no lead, either of which would leave the two phases inseparable
hypothesis: the class splits between analysis and preparation, and the split is decidable offline from the cause and the displaced draft the scorer already records
intervention: grouped every place and unled must-find loss of the 6bff717 Baseline, scored against the corpus at HEAD, by cause and by whether a displaced draft exists
reconsider_when: a second sweep gives the split a spread, or the candidate rules change, which moves which references are led
scope: 27 place and unled must-find losses of one sweep against the corpus at HEAD. place means a rule led the lane to the reference's elements, so preparation is ruled out for those rows by the cause definition itself. Split: place 20 (18 with a displaced draft, 2 without), unled 7 (3 with, 4 without). Analysis owns 20 of 27 and preparation at most 7. One sweep, so no row carries a spread.
signature: the lane writes near the reference and not at it, which is the place and unled class

falsifier: the maintainer's votes rule the displaced drafts real, which would make the class a selection problem rather than a correctness one
hypothesis: the displaced draft is a wrong finding, so the class is the lane writing nonsense at a neighbouring element
intervention: joined all 21 displaced must-find rows to the vote ledger on case, endpoint-resolved elements and verb, and read every note
reconsider_when: a second voter rules the same drafts, or the sitting converts any of the 16 into reference claims
scope: 21 displaced must-find rows of one sweep, one voter, sitting web-42e98b49. 16 ruled up, 3 down as duplicate, 1 down as wrong-lane, 1 needs-evidence. A positive control joins 182 of the sweep's 195 drafts, so the lookup is sound. In 17 of the 21 the reference and the draft each name two elements and share exactly one, so the lane held the anchor and wrote the wrong counterparty. Says nothing about a second voter or a second sweep.
signature: the lane writes near the reference and not at it, which is the place and unled class

falsifier: a lane that already drafts at more places than it is led to still loses must-finds, or the lanes with the most untouched leads are the ones losing least
hypothesis: one instruction to draft at every led place answers the class, because the class is the lane stopping short of the leads it receives
intervention: ran the stride candidate rules over all 13 blessed models, counted the distinct endpoint-resolved places each lane is led to, and set that beside the places the 6bff717 Baseline drafted at and the places the corpus lists
reconsider_when: a rule is added or removed, which moves the lead counts, or a second sweep gives the drafted counts a spread
scope: 13 blessed models for the lead half, one sweep for the drafted half. Led, drafted and listed per lane: information-disclosure 112/58/56, repudiation 64/20/28, tampering 61/36/56, spoofing 31/34/49, denial-of-service 28/19/35, elevation-of-privilege 14/15/18. A blanket instruction grows output 182 places to 310, and 98 of the 128 new places land in information-disclosure and repudiation, which between them lose 5 of the 43 must-finds. Spoofing and elevation-of-privilege already draft at more places than they are led to and lose 17 between them, so neither has a volume shortfall to close. The lead counts are a property of the rules and the corpus and carry no run-to-run spread; the drafted counts are one sweep and do.
signature: a lane is led to a place by a candidate rule and files no draft there, which the scorer charges as place

falsifier: the scorer's own standing per draft disagrees with the hand-join, which would mean the join read votes the scorer excludes
hypothesis: the hand-join of -E3 counted the right thing, so 16 of the 21 displaced must-find rows carry a person's acceptance
intervention: added `displaced_standing` to the loss row, read from the scorer's own CaseScore.unlisted by draft ID, and re-scored the 6bff717 Baseline against the corpus at HEAD
reconsider_when: a sitting votes the displaced drafts, which moves open and stale into a standing that answers
scope: the same 21 displaced must-find rows. The instrument reads matched 9, pooled 8, rejected 1, open 1, stale 2. The hand-join of -E3 was wrong twice: it counted votes on drafts the scorer had matched to a reference of their own, where the ledger is never asked, and it collapsed open and stale into an acceptance. The headline survives on firmer ground — 17 of the 21 sit beside a draft the corpus itself lists or a person pooled, and exactly 1 beside a rejected one. Over all 64 displaced rows: matched 30, pooled 16, rejected 6, open 6, stale 6.
signature: the lane writes near the reference and not at it, which is the place and unled class

falsifier: the trigger test is looser than a place-level match, which would mean a place row can fire on a candidate about somewhere else
hypothesis: a `place` row means the lane was offered the reference's place as a candidate, so analysis owns it and preparation cannot
intervention: read `evals.harness.triggers._hit`, then asked per `place` must-find whether any candidate in the lane names the reference's endpoint-resolved place as a set
reconsider_when: a rule is added, which changes which places carry a candidate, or `_hit` is tightened to a place-level match
scope: 20 `place` must-find rows of the 6bff717 Baseline against the corpus at HEAD. `_hit` matches on lane plus element overlap and is documented as deliberately loose, so one rule firing on one element the reference names makes the row `place`. Only 7 of the 20 have a candidate at the reference's place as a set: tampering 3 of 8, spoofing 2 of 4, elevation-of-privilege 1 of 2, denial-of-service 0 of 5, repudiation 0 of 1. So preparation owns the other 13: the lane was never offered that place. -E2 stated analysis owns 20 of 27 and that is wrong; analysis owns at most 7 of the 20 `place` rows.
signature: a lane is led to a place by a candidate rule and files no draft there, which the scorer charges as place

falsifier: the reachable losses number fewer than the band, which no run of any size could read
hypothesis: the instruction clears the run-to-run band, so a paid run can see it
intervention: priced the instruction on the rows it can reach: a tampering `place` must-find with a candidate at the reference's own place
reconsider_when: the tampering rules propose the places the references name, which is what -E6 says is missing, and the ceiling is re-read after that
scope: 8 tampering `place` must-finds. Only 3 carry a candidate at the reference's place, so the ceiling is 3 of 103, which is 2.9 points against a corpus band of about 3.3. The audit's first pricing read 8 and 7.8 points, because it took `place` to mean a place-level lead; -E6 shows it does not. No single case can see it either: the 8 spread over 7 cases, at most 2 in one, against a per-case must-find spread near 0.8. Case 10 carries 2 of the 8 and its tampering lane already drafts at every place it is led to.
signature: the tampering lane is led to 61 places and drafts at 36, so an instruction to use its leads recovers its place losses

falsifier: the matcher accepts a containment, which would make a candidate wider than the reference a lead at a coarser grain
hypothesis: a candidate must name the reference's place exactly to count as a lead, so 14 of the 20 place must-finds were never led
intervention: measured each place must-find at three grains: a candidate equal to the reference's endpoint-resolved place, a candidate the matcher's own endpoint_subset accepts, and element overlap alone
reconsider_when: the identity rule stops accepting a containment, or a rule is added, which moves which places carry a candidate
scope: 20 place must-finds of the 6bff717 Baseline against the corpus at HEAD. Exact 6, subset a further 6, overlap only 8. endpoint_subset is the rule the scorer already matches drafts with, and its docstring gives the reason: two sides written at different grain are one claim. So analysis owns 12 and preparation owns 8, not the 7 and 13 of -E6. -E6 also miscounted the exact tier as 7 where the rows sum to 6.
signature: a lane is led to a place by a candidate rule and files no draft there, which the scorer charges as place

falsifier: led and unled must-finds match at the same rate, which would price every new rule at zero however many places it reaches
hypothesis: a lead converts, so the gain from a new rule can be priced from the rate at which led references are matched
intervention: for all 103 must-find references, asked whether any candidate in the lane satisfies endpoint_subset against it, and crossed that with whether the Baseline matched it
reconsider_when: a second sweep gives the two rates a spread, or a new rule lands and its own newly led references are scored apart
scope: 103 must-find references, one sweep. Led 50 of 75 matched, rate 0.667. Not led 10 of 28 matched, rate 0.357. The gap is 0.31. This is a correlation and an upper bound on what a new rule buys: the existing rules fire on structurally obvious places, so the led group is the easier group, and a rule reaching a harder reference need not convert at 0.667. QA-2026-09-20-01-E16 measured that directly - it added four leads, three of which named a flow the claim was not about, and bought about one must-find.
signature: a candidate rule leading the lane to a place changes whether the lane finds the reference there

falsifier: the reachable rows times the measured conversion lift come to fewer must-finds than the band
hypothesis: one new rule family clears the run-to-run band, so it can be measured on its own
intervention: listed every missed must-find with no candidate at or containing its place, grouped them by the element types they name, and priced each group at the 0.31 conversion lift -E9 measured
reconsider_when: the two families are prototyped and their own lead rate and mechanism match are read, which is what decides whether the 0.31 applies to them at all
scope: 18 missed must-finds the rules never point at. Three are out of a lead's reach - two lost to verb and one to the critic, where the lane already wrote at the place - leaving 15. Two families: an actor and the store it touches, 9 reachable rows, and an actor and a process, 6 reachable rows. Priced at 0.31 each: the store family buys about 2.8 must-finds and the process family about 1.9, both inside the corpus band of 3.37. Together they buy about 4.7, which clears it 1.4 times over. So neither family may be measured alone and the two must land together. The 4.7 is an upper bound for the reason -E9 gives.
signature: the candidate rules never point at some missed must-finds, so a new rule family recovers them

falsifier: the shape is already covered and declined for a stated reason, or the two elements carry no flow a rule over flows could fire on
hypothesis: a new rule proposes the place, because the shape is one the rules do not cover
intervention: read the flows between the two elements of each of the 10 store rows, against _unverified_write_to_store, which already yields exactly this shape
reconsider_when: the assertion layer carries an authority predicate a rule can read, which is the order #671 finding 11 asks for, or a reachability rule over paths is written
scope: 10 missed must-finds naming a store with no candidate at or containing their place. 6 carry a flow inside the place and every one of the 6 reads `operations == "read"`, which _unverified_write_to_store skips on purpose: its docstring records the decision, names three of these losses and gives the reason - the references rest on the store being unauthenticated at all, which is authority rather than operations and no model field carries it. The other 4 carry no flow between the two elements, so the claim is about a multi-hop path and a rule over single flows cannot state that place. No rule was written.
signature: a missed must-find names an actor and the store it touches, and no candidate rule proposes that place

falsifier: the rule's leads name a flow the claim is not about, or it adds candidates out of proportion to the must-finds it reaches
hypothesis: a rule firing on an unverified flow into a process leads these references and clears the band
intervention: prototyped the predicate offline over the 13 blessed models, counted the candidates it adds, and read each newly led reference against the flow it fired on
reconsider_when: a rule keys on authorization rather than authentication, which is the fact case 11 and case 06's elevation actually rest on
scope: 13 blessed models, elevation-of-privilege and spoofing. The rule adds 29 candidate places on the 52 those two lanes already carry, nearly tripling elevation-of-privilege from 15 to 35. It newly leads 4 must-finds. On QA-2026-09-20-01-E16's own test - does the rule name the very flow the claim is about - one is a clean match, case 06's forged match hand-over; one names the right flow for the wrong reason, case 11, where the rule reads authentication and the claim is about role separation; and two name a different flow entirely, case 06's elevation, whose mechanism is the onward grant to the player database, and case 08's, whose mechanism is the nightly pull's latency. Priced at -E9's 0.31 lift that is 0.3 to 0.6 must-finds against a corpus band of 3.37. No rule was written.
signature: a missed must-find names an actor and a process, and no candidate rule proposes that place
